answer: Randomized Shard Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function assigns every agent to a shard sealed until the epoch opens; work rewards flow only through cross-shard marble checkpoints. An attacker must predict shard seats before committing resources, so each fake identity needs fresh copper deposits for bandwidth and latency to synchronize with unknown peers. Because assignments reshuffle unpredictably, pre-building karst-like infrastructure across all shards costs roughly N times a single identity's overhead.
